channel.title: A History of Christianity
channel.description: A spoken history of Christianity in forty chapters, from Second Temple Judaism and the historical Jesus to the present: doctrine, heresy and empire, East and West, medieval Christendom, Reformation, mission and empire, and the twentieth century. Seasons follow the eight Parts; the annexes on saints and holidays are bonus episodes.
channel.itunes:author: Study
channel.itunes:summary: A spoken history of Christianity in forty chapters, from Second Temple Judaism and the historical Jesus to the present: doctrine, heresy and empire, East and West, medieval Christendom, Reformation, mission and empire, and the twentieth century. Seasons follow the eight Parts; the annexes on saints and holidays are bonus episodes.
channel.itunes:subtitle: From the Second Temple to the Present

item.title: 1. Second Temple Judaism and the Historical Jesus: What Can Be Known
item.description: The Problem of Sources; Methods and Their Limits; Second Temple Judaism: The World Jesus Inhabited; Jesus of Nazareth: A Sketch Within the Evidence.

item.title: 2. Paul, the Gentile Mission, and the Earliest Communities
item.description: The Earliest Jerusalem Community; Saul of Tarsus; The Gentile Mission and Its Theological Logic; The Shape of the Pauline Mission.

item.title: 3. Persecution, Apologetics, and the Church Within the Roman Empire
item.description: A Movement Without Legal Standing; The Pattern of Persecution: Local, Sporadic, and Later Systematic; The Apologists: Defending the Faith to a Hostile World; Institutional Consolidation Under Pressure; The Martyr's Grave and the Origins of the Cult of Saints.

item.title: 4. Scripture, Canon, and Authority: How the Bible Took Shape
item.description: The Hebrew Bible and the Question of "Old Testament"; The Formation of the New Testament Canon; Canon, Authority, and the Question Reformation Would Later Reopen; Textual Transmission: How the Words Themselves Survived.

item.title: 5. Core Doctrine I: God, Trinity, Incarnation, and Salvation
item.description: Monotheism Under Pressure: The Problem the Doctrine of the Trinity Solves; The Vocabulary of Trinitarian Definition; The Incarnation: God Become Human; Soteriology: How Does Christ's Death and Resurrection Save?.

item.title: 6. Core Doctrine II: Sacraments, the Eucharist, and Transubstantiation
item.description: What a Sacrament Is; Baptism: Incorporation and Cleansing; The Eucharist: Institution and Early Understanding; Transubstantiation: The Aristotelian Framework.

item.title: 7. Core Doctrine III: Sin, Grace, Purgatory, and the Afterlife
item.description: Original Sin: A Doctrine and Its Disputed Foundations; Grace, Merit, and the Larger Western Synthesis; Purgatory: Origins and Function; Heaven, Hell, and the Wider Eschatological Picture; Angels: The Celestial Hierarchy; The Devil: From Adversary to Cosmic Enemy.

item.title: 8. Church, Hierarchy, and Authority: Bishops, Councils, and Apostolic Succession
item.description: From Plural Leadership to Monepiscopacy; Apostolic Succession: The Theological Claim; Councils: Conciliar Authority and Its Theory; The Petrine Claim and the Question of Roman Primacy.

item.title: 9. Gnosticism, Marcion, and the Definition of Orthodoxy
item.description: The Problem of Naming; The Nag Hammadi Library and What It Changed; Marcion: A Distinct Case; Irenaeus and the Construction of Orthodoxy; The Limits of Repression and the Persistence of Gnosis.

item.title: 10. Constantine, Nicaea, and the Arian Controversy
item.description: Constantine: The Conversion and Its Historiographical Problems; The Church After Toleration: A New Set of Problems; Arius and the Controversy Before Nicaea; The Council of Nicaea, 325; The Long Aftermath: Arianism After Nicaea.

item.title: 11. Donatism, North Africa, and the Politics of Purity
item.description: North Africa and the Church Before the Schism; The Traditores and the Succession Dispute; Constantine and the Failure of Imperial Settlement; The Circumcellions: Class, Violence, and the Limits of Ecclesiastical Control; Augustine and the Turn to Coercion.

item.title: 12. Augustine versus Pelagius: Grace, Free Will, and a Political Church
item.description: Augustine of Hippo: The Mind Behind the Controversy; The Question of Free Will: Setting Up the Problem; Pelagius: The Position and Its Appeal; Augustine's Response: Grace, Predestination, and the Bound Will; The Political Dimension: From Theological Dispute to Imperial Condemnation; The Augustinian Legacy and Its Ambivalence.

item.title: 13. Nestorius, Cyril, and the Christological Wars: The Road to Ephesus
item.description: Two Schools and Their Different Instincts; Nestorius: The Man and the Controversy; Cyril of Alexandria: Theology and Power; The Council of Ephesus, 431: Procedure as Weapon; The Theological Residue of Ephesus.

item.title: 14. Chalcedon and the Making of the Miaphysite Churches
item.description: The Problem Ephesus Left Unsolved; Leo's Tome and the Western Position; The Council of Chalcedon, 451; The Miaphysite Rejection and the Permanent Schism.

item.title: 15. Global Spread, Phase One: Byzantium, Armenia, Ethiopia, and the Church of the East to China
item.description: Christianity as a Multipolar Phenomenon; Byzantium: The Christian Empire of the East; Armenia: The First Christian Nation; Ethiopia: Christianity in the Kingdom of Aksum; The Church of the East: Christianity Beyond Rome; The Significance of This Diversity.

item.title: 16. Monasticism: Benedict, the Desert Fathers, and the Shaping of Western Christendom
item.description: The Impulse and Its Context; The Desert Fathers: Egypt and the Anachoretic Tradition; Pachomius and the Cenobitic Alternative; Basil and the Eastern Synthesis; Benedict of Nursia and the Western Synthesis; The Political Economy of Monasticism; Monasticism and the Transmission of Knowledge.

item.title: 17. Conversion of the North: Franks, Anglo-Saxons, and the Carolingian Church
item.description: Conversion as Political Event; Clovis and the Frankish Conversion; Ireland and the Peregrini: Monasticism as Mission; The Anglo-Saxon Mission and the Roman Model; Charlemagne and the Carolingian Church.

item.title: 18. Iconoclasm and the Byzantine Crisis
item.description: Images and Their Contested Place in Christian Devotion; The Origins of Imperial Iconoclasm; The Course of the Controversy; Monasticism, Resistance, and the Reconfiguration of Authority; Iconoclasm and the Estrangement of Rome.

item.title: 19. The Filioque, Rome versus Constantinople, and the Schism of 1054
item.description: A Schism in Slow Motion; The Filioque: A Theological Dispute and Its History; Diverging Ecclesiologies: The Structural Incompatibility; The Photian Schism and the Ninth-Century Crisis; 1054: The Trigger and Its Limits; The Fourth Crusade's Shadow: 1204 and the Real Wound.

item.title: 20. Gregorian Reform and the Investiture Controversy: Church versus Empire
item.description: The Problem of a Church Embedded in Feudal Power; Cluny and the Monastic Origins of Reform; Leo IX and the Reform Papacy; Gregory VII: The Theology of Reform; The Investiture Contest: Henry IV and the Road to Canossa; The Longer Consequences.

item.title: 21. The Crusades: Origins, Aims, and the Sack of Constantinople
item.description: What Were the Crusades?; The Background: Holy War, Pilgrimage, and the Devotional World; Urban II at Clermont, 1095: The Appeal and Its Ambiguities; The First Crusade and Jerusalem's Fall: 1096–1099; Bernard of Clairvaux: The Conscience of the Twelfth Century; Saladin, the Loss of Jerusalem, and the Later Crusades; The Anti-Jewish Violence of the Crusades; The Crusades in Historical Perspective.

item.title: 22. Heresy and Repression: Cathars, the Albigensian Crusade, and the Inquisition
item.description: The Cathar Movement: What It Was and What It Was Not; The Political Geography of the Languedoc; The Inquisition: Origins, Methods, and Realities; The Destruction of Catharism and Its Lessons.

item.title: 23. Scholasticism: Aquinas and the Marriage of Faith and Reason
item.description: The Institutional Revolution: The Rise of the Universities; The Recovery of Aristotle and Its Consequences; Thomas Aquinas: The Synthesis; The Condemnations of 1277 and the Limits of Synthesis.

item.title: 24. The Church and the Jews: The Origins of Institutional Christian Antisemitism
item.description: Framing: Theology, History, and Moral Responsibility; The Patristic Roots: Supersessionism and the Adversus Judaeos Tradition; The Charge of Deicide and Its Consequences; The Institutional Architecture of Mediaeval Jewish Subjugation; The Black Death and the Accusations of Well-Poisoning; Forward Threads: Luther and the Holocaust.

item.title: 25. Avignon, Schism, and the Conciliar Crisis
item.description: The Road to Avignon: Boniface VIII and the Overreach of Papal Power; Avignon: The Captive Papacy?; The Great Western Schism: Three Popes and a Broken Church; The Conciliar Movement: A Constitutional Theory of Church Governance; Jan Hus and the Council's Moral Failure; The Conciliar Movement's Defeat and Its Consequences.

item.title: 26. Heresy Before Luther: Wycliffe, Hus, and the Limits of Dissent
item.description: Why These Movements Matter; John Wycliffe: Scripture, Dominion, and the Attack on the Church; Jan Hus: Bohemia and the Politicisation of Reform; Why the Limits Held — And Why They Would Not Hold for Luther.
